result.title: SMAD: A Semantics-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Unsupervised Time-Series Anomaly Detection
result.summary: Time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) lacks a one-size-fits-all detector for heterogeneous data and anomaly types. Existing automation is limited by implicit objectives, potentially unreliable historical knowledge, or high computational costs. More fundamentally, it selects how to detect anomalies without explicitly defining what to detect. We propose SMAD, an LLM-based multi-agent framework that translates anomaly intent into executable, testable detection pipelines. Rather than selecting detectors against an implicit target, SMAD establishes a natural-language semantic contract grounded in measurable time-series properties, specifying target event patterns, expected score responses, and validation questions. This contract governs both detector construction and evaluation: LLM agents propose pipelines, while contract-matched synthetic interventions provide label-free evidence from the target series to assess semantic coverage and guide iterative self-refinement. A semantics-aware ensemble integrates validated candidates and attributes each alert to contributing detectors and supporting evidence. On univariate and multivariate TSAD benchmarks, SMAD improves detection performance over the strongest baseline by 11.5% and 9.6%, respectively, while outperforming general-purpose coding agents at 2-5x lower language-model token cost.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 SMAD，一个基于 LLM 多智能体的无监督时间序列异常检测框架：先用自然语言「语义契约」明确要检测的目标事件模式与验证问题，再由智能体生成检测流水线，并以契约匹配的合成干预提供无标签证据进行迭代自改进和语义感知集成。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「把要检测什么显式写成契约、再用合成干预作为无标签证据并归因到具体组件」的思路，可能与 LVR 中验证问题的定义、视觉证据筛选与贡献分配有概念联系，可供核查；但领域相距较远，迁移性未知。
